q: Why won't a CBAM verifier quote a fixed fee?
title: Why CBAM verifiers avoid fixed fees
short: Because accreditation rules do not let verifiers accept lump sum contracts. If errors turn up, the verifier must widen its sampling, and that extra work has to be paid for. A fixed price would put pressure on its independence. A strong control system keeps the work, and the bill, down.
audience: Indian operators budgeting for CBAM verification

ul: The number of production processes and precursors.
The quality of your data flow and controls.
Contract a verifier early in the year.
Keep fuel, power and production records traceable to source documents.
Run your own review before the verifier arrives.

senseible: Senseible keeps the invoices behind each fuel and electricity figure in one fingerprinted record, so a verifier can sample them without a hunt through files. Senseible is not a CBAM verifier and does not issue verification reports.
